mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thus driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If 20-day returns are not higher during easing periods, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns remain positive despite unemployment rise.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth indicates weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive with slow GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent slowdown in GDP and housing starts indicates weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive with both proxies slowing.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production indicates supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive despite production slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment suggests inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive with employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate and falling unemployment indicate tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive with both conditions met.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing real estate investment in late-cycle expansion signals weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive with slow real estate investment.
